messages:
Maria: FYI escalation from Kevin at Streamline — they saw intermittent 429s and 4-6s tail latency hitting their dedicated pool d-cap-42 starting ~10:20 UTC. Customer says it started after a spike in traffic, but timeline shows continuous scale up/down cycles.
Jamal: Thx — can you paste the scale event log and perf graphs? link?
Maria: Link: https://console.redwood.internal/dedicated/d-cap-42/metrics?range=1h
Maria: Quick paste of the autoscaler events (truncated):
```
2026-01-15T10:18:30Z autoscaler[d-cap-42] scale_to 6 (util 0.84)
2026-01-15T10:19:02Z autoscaler[d-cap-42] scale_to 3 (util 0.12)
2026-01-15T10:19:58Z autoscaler[d-cap-42] scale_to 7 (util 0.91)
2026-01-15T10:20:35Z autoscaler[d-cap-42] scale_to 2 (util 0.10)
...
```
Maria: Also seeing a correlated burst in request QPS + short-lived GPU mem pressure spikes in the runtime logs. Some tenants show heavy bursts while others are idle.
Lin: That pattern smells like oscillation: bursts push util > scale_up_threshold -> scale up -> burst ends -> scale down immediately. If cooldown/stabilization window is too small we'll thrash. What's the current autoscaler config for the pool?
Maria: Current config (from prod):
```yaml
pool: d-cap-42
min_replicas: 0
max_replicas: 12
scale_up_threshold: 0.75
scale_down_threshold: 0.25
scale_up_cooldown_s: 30
scale_down_cooldown_s: 30
stabilization_window_s: 45
metric: avg_gpu_utilization
```
Kevin: Streamline also called out a sudden billing bump — they saw a 3x charge for that window. They want mitigation asap and a credit while we stabilize.
Olga: Oncall suggestion: quick mitigation — set `min_replicas: 2` for the pool and bump `scale_down_cooldown_s` to 120s so we avoid immediate scale-down after a burst. That will reduce thrash and give us breathing room.
Jamal: Agree. Also recommend switching metric to `request_queue_length` or adding a smoothing window on util. Avg_gpu_utilization is noisy with short bursts. Proposed change:
```yaml
min_replicas: 2
stabilization_window_s: 120
scale_up_cooldown_s: 30
scale_down_cooldown_s: 120
scale_up_threshold: 0.8
scale_down_threshold: 0.2
metric: smoothed_gpu_utilization (avg over 30s window)
```
Lin: We should also consider per-tenant rate limiting. Noisy neighbor is obvious — a single tenant's burst is driving whole pool. For a safer short-term step, enable tenant-level QPS caps on Streamline's key while we tune autoscaler.
Maria: Repro steps I used: lightweight k6 script that issues 10s bursts every 20s to the dedicated endpoint (makes oscillation pretty deterministic). Example command: `k6 run --vus 200 --duration 1m burst_test.js` where `burst_test.js` ramps VUs in 10s pulses. I can attach the script if useful.
Jamal: Please attach. Also add the exact request pattern (payload size, sequence length) — LLM token size affects GPU time. If customers are sending long sequences during bursts, that explains the high util spikes.
Maria: Attached script in thread (pasted):
```js
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export default function () {
  http.post('https://api.redwood.company/dedicated/d-cap-42/generate', JSON.stringify({input: 'token-heavy payload ~2k chars'}), { headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer <streamline-key>' } });
  sleep(0.1);
}
// run with: k6 run --vus 200 --duration 1m
```
Srinivas: Ops note: changing min_replicas + cooling is low-risk. We should run the change in staging with the same autoscaler image and metrics aggregation configuration, then roll to prod during a low-impact window. I'll create a change request and link to a canary job.
DeployBot: Change request created: CR-2147 by srinivas — includes rollout plan, staging validation, and rollback steps.
Srinivas: I'll also add a metric to detect "high-frequency scale events" (count of scale actions > 3 in 5m) and alert on it so we can auto-detect flapping pools.
Kevin: I'll tell Streamline we will set min_replicas=2 and pause aggressive downscaling, and offer a credit for the billing spike. Keep me posted so I can update them.
Jamal: Action items: 1) Apply temporary config (min_replicas=2, scale_down_cooldown_s=120) to d-cap-42 and monitor for 30m — Jamal owns. 2) Tune metrics/stabilization and add smoothing for avg util — Lin owns. 3) Add tenant QPS cap and coordinate with CS for keys — Maria/Kevin. 4) Create alert for scale-flap metric — Srinivas.
Olga: @Jamal, can you patch before 11:15 UTC? Customer is affected now.
Jamal: I'll push the config change to prod in 10m and watch the dashboard. Will post back with results. :eyes:
Maria: Thanks everyone. I will keep Streamline updated. :thumbsup:
Jamal: Update 10m after change: no more scale-to-zero events, tail latency dropped from ~4.8s -> ~0.9s, error rate 429 -> near 0. Keeping monitoring for 45m.
Maria: Customer confirmed improved performance and appreciated the quick mitigation. Kevin — please proceed with the credit plan.
Srinivas: Follow-up: we'll schedule a deeper root cause postmortem next week to decide long-term changes (smoothing defaults, autoscaler algorithm tweak, per-tenant isolation knobs).
